title: [Phase 9] Remove HLS fallback delivery path (WHEP-only)
body:
## Goal

Remove the HLS fallback delivery path once WHEP is validated at scale, simplifying the architecture and reducing MediaMTX resource usage.

## Background

WHEP (WebRTC) is now the **primary** listener delivery path with sub-second latency. HLS was the original delivery mechanism but adds complexity (port 8888, HLS config in mediamtx.yml, listener template, env vars). Once WHEP is validated in production, HLS can be fully removed.

## Prerequisites

WHEP must be validated with:
- 50+ concurrent listeners on a production deployment
- Cross-browser testing (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
- iOS Safari WHEP playback confirmed
- Handoff tested with real interpreters at a live event
- At least one production event successfully uses WHEP as the sole listener path

## Removal Steps

| Step | Action | Files affected |
|------|--------|----------------|
| 1 | Remove HLS listener route from FastAPI | `fastapi_app.py` — delete `/listen/{booth_id}` route |
| 2 | Delete HLS listener template | `templates/listener.html` — delete file |
| 3 | Remove HLS config from MediaMTX | `mediamtx.yml` — remove `hlsAddress`, `hlsEncryption`, `hlsAlwaysRemux`, `hlsSegmentDuration`, `hlsSegmentMaxSize`, `hlsAllowOrigins` |
| 4 | Remove HLS port from Docker Compose | `docker-compose.yml` — remove `8888:8888` port mapping |
| 5 | Remove `MEDIAMTX_HLS_BASE` env var | `portal/config.py`, `.env`, `docker-compose.yml` |
| 6 | Update reverse proxy config | Remove HLS proxy rules from Caddyfile/nginx |
| 7 | Remove HLS references from docs | `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` — update architecture diagrams, port tables, env var tables |
| 8 | Update Eventyay integration | `StreamSchedule.config` — remove `hls` field from `interpretation_tracks`, keep only `whep` |
| 9 | Remove LL-HLS references | `mediamtx.yml` — remove `hlsPartDuration` comments |
| 10 | Remove hls.js fallback from viewer | `interpretation-player.js` — remove HLS playback code |
| 11 | Run full test suite | `uv run pytest tests/ -v` |

## Port Simplification After HLS Removal

| Port | Protocol | Service | Status |
|------|----------|---------|--------|
| 8889 | TCP | WHIP/WHEP signaling | **Kept** |
| 8189 | UDP | WebRTC ICE/RTP | **Kept** |
| 8888 | TCP | HLS playlists/segments | **Removed** |
| 9997 | TCP | Control API | **Kept** |

## Tasks

- [ ] Validate WHEP with 50+ concurrent listeners
- [ ] Confirm iOS Safari WHEP playback
- [ ] Test handoff with real interpreters at live event
- [ ] Remove `/listen/{booth_id}` route from `fastapi_app.py`
- [ ] Delete `templates/listener.html`
- [ ] Remove HLS config from `mediamtx.yml`
- [ ] Remove port 8888 from `docker-compose.yml`
- [ ] Remove `MEDIAMTX_HLS_BASE` from `portal/config.py`
- [ ] Update reverse proxy config
- [ ] Remove HLS references from all documentation
- [ ] Update Eventyay StreamSchedule integration to WHEP-only
- [ ] Remove hls.js fallback from viewer page
- [ ] Run full test suite

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- All previous phases complete
- WHEP validated in production

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No HLS code remains in the codebase
- [ ] MediaMTX no longer serves on port 8888
- [ ] All listener paths use WHEP exclusively
- [ ] Eventyay viewer integration uses WHEP endpoints
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Production event successfully runs WHEP-only
- [ ] Documentation updated (no HLS references remain)

## Out of Scope

- TURN server for restrictive networks (separate issue)
- Recording/archive functionality

title: CI/CD, Testing, and Deployment Hardening
body:
## CI/CD, Testing, and Deployment Hardening

**Goal:** Robust CI pipeline, comprehensive test coverage, automated linting, WHIP auth. This phase happens **after Phase 4** (stable UX) and **before Phase 7** (latency reduction) — you need reliable CI to safely refactor MediaMTX config.

### 9.1 Expand Test Coverage

**Current:** 154+ tests covering REST API, WebSocket protocol, auth, booth state, booth identity, multi-event namespace isolation, and handoff scenarios.

| Area | Tests to add |
|---|---|
| Database CRUD | Event/Room/Booth/Token model operations (Phase 3) |
| RBAC enforcement | Role-route combinations, 401/403 for all endpoints |
| Admin panel | Template rendering, CRUD operations |
| Template rendering | All config variables populated, no Jinja2 errors |
| Config validation | Invalid/missing env vars |
| JavaScript (future) | WHIP flow mocking, WebSocket protocol via Playwright |

### 9.2 Linting and Code Quality

Add to `tests.yml`:

```yaml
- name: Lint Python (ruff)
  run: uv run ruff check .

- name: Format check (ruff)
  run: uv run ruff format --check .

- name: Type check (pyright)
  run: uv run pyright fastapi_app.py portal/
```

Add to `pyproject.toml` dev group: `ruff`, `pyright`.

### 9.3 Docker Build CI

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
name: Docker Build
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop, dev]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: docker build -t interp-portal-test .
      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          docker run -d --name test -p 8000:8000 \
            -e SECRET_KEY=test -e HOST=0.0.0.0 \
            interp-portal-test
          sleep 5
          curl -f http://localhost:8000/healthz
          docker stop test
```

### 9.4 Dependabot Strategy

| Ecosystem | Auto-merge? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **pip** (Python packages) | No — pytest must pass first | Recheck if FastAPI/Pydantic changes are breaking |
| **github-actions** | Safe to auto-merge minor bumps | Manual for major version bumps |
| **docker** (Jitsi, MediaMTX) | **Never auto-merge** | Always test Jitsi iframe + MediaMTX WHIP/WHEP manually after any bump |

**Jitsi image bumps are the riskiest.** All 4 Jitsi images must be bumped together (same `stable-XXXX` tag). CI passes even if Jitsi is broken because tests don't spin up Jitsi containers — always test manually before merging Jitsi PRs.

### 9.5 WHIP Authentication

Prevent unauthorized browsers from publishing to MediaMTX paths.

**Option A (recommended):** MediaMTX external auth webhook

```yaml
# mediamtx.yml
pathDefaults:
  runOnPublish: |
    curl -f -X POST http://portal:8000/api/internal/whip-auth \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MEDIAMTX_INTERNAL_TOKEN}" \
      -d '{"path":"$MTX_PATH"}'
  runOnPublishRestart: no
```

**Option B:** Short-lived bearer token in WHIP POST
- FastAPI `/api/booth/{id}/whip-token` returns a one-time JWT
- Browser includes `Authorization: Bearer <token>` in WHIP POST
- MediaMTX validates via `publishPass` external auth

### 9.6 Success Criteria

- [ ] CI runs: pytest, ruff lint, ruff format check, pyright, Docker build
- [ ] Test coverage > 80% for `fastapi_app.py` and `portal/`
- [ ] Dependabot PRs tested according to strategy above
- [ ] WHIP auth prevents unauthorized publishing

---

title: [Phase 1][Step 9] Self-Hosted Jitsi Meet
body:
# Self-Hosted Jitsi Meet

After Phase 1D completes the Flask→FastAPI migration, add a self-hosted Jitsi Meet instance to the Docker Compose stack. Currently, the interpreter booth embeds the public `meet.jit.si` service for the interpreter to watch/hear the speaker. Self-hosting Jitsi gives full control and removes the external dependency.

**Why self-host Jitsi:**
- **No external dependency** — the portal stack is fully self-contained
- **Same Docker Compose** — single `docker compose up` starts everything
- **Room name parity** — the `DEFAULT_JITSI_ROOM` config creates rooms on the local Jitsi instance, so the booth embed and the speaker's Jitsi room are on the same server
- **Privacy** — no audio/video data leaves your infrastructure
- **Custom branding** — watermark, welcome page, and UI can be configured

**Services to add to `docker-compose.yml`:**

```yaml
  # ── Jitsi Meet (self-hosted video conferencing) ───────────────
  jitsi-web:
    image: jitsi/web:stable
    ports:
      - "8443:443"    # Jitsi HTTPS UI
    environment:
      - ENABLE_AUTH=0
      - ENABLE_GUESTS=1
      - PUBLIC_URL=https://jitsi.your-domain.com
      - TZ=UTC
      - XMPP_DOMAIN=meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_AUTH_DOMAIN=auth.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_BOSH_URL_BASE=http://xmpp.meet.jitsi:5280
      - XMPP_MUC_DOMAIN=muc.meet.jitsi
    depends_on:
      - jitsi-prosody
    restart: unless-stopped

  jitsi-prosody:
    image: jitsi/prosody:stable
    environment:
      - XMPP_DOMAIN=meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_AUTH_DOMAIN=auth.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_MUC_DOMAIN=muc.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_INTERNAL_MUC_DOMAIN=internal-muc.meet.jitsi
      - JVB_AUTH_USER=jvb
      - JVB_AUTH_PASSWORD=${JVB_AUTH_PASSWORD:-changeme}
      - JICOFO_AUTH_USER=focus
      - JICOFO_AUTH_PASSWORD=${JICOFO_AUTH_PASSWORD:-changeme}
      - TZ=UTC
    restart: unless-stopped

  jitsi-jicofo:
    image: jitsi/jicofo:stable
    environment:
      - XMPP_DOMAIN=meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_AUTH_DOMAIN=auth.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_INTERNAL_MUC_DOMAIN=internal-muc.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_MUC_DOMAIN=muc.meet.jitsi
      - JICOFO_AUTH_USER=focus
      - JICOFO_AUTH_PASSWORD=${JICOFO_AUTH_PASSWORD:-changeme}
      - TZ=UTC
    depends_on:
      - jitsi-prosody
    restart: unless-stopped

  jitsi-jvb:
    image: jitsi/jvb:stable
    ports:
      - "10000:10000/udp"  # JVB media traffic
    environment:
      - XMPP_AUTH_DOMAIN=auth.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_INTERNAL_MUC_DOMAIN=internal-muc.meet.jitsi
      - XMPP_DOMAIN=meet.jitsi
      - JVB_AUTH_USER=jvb
      - JVB_AUTH_PASSWORD=${JVB_AUTH_PASSWORD:-changeme}
      - JVB_PORT=10000
      - JVB_STUN_SERVERS=stun:stun.l.google.com:19302
      - TZ=UTC
    depends_on:
      - jitsi-prosody
    restart: unless-stopped
```

**Portal config changes:**
- `JITSI_DOMAIN` changes from `meet.jit.si` to `localhost:8443` (dev) or `jitsi.your-domain.com` (prod)
- `DEFAULT_JITSI_ROOM` stays the same — the room name is created on the local Jitsi instance
- The interpreter booth iframe `src` already uses `JITSI_DOMAIN` so no frontend code changes are needed

**When to implement:** After Phase 1D (Flask removal) is merged. This is an additive feature — it does not require any changes to the portal code, only Docker Compose configuration.

### Why Incremental?

- **No big-bang rewrite.** Flask keeps working while FastAPI is validated.
- **Each phase is independently deployable and testable.**
- **Rollback is trivial** — just switch back to the Flask entry point.
- **MediaMTX integration (Phase 1A) does not depend on the Flask→FastAPI migration** — it only needs the frontend to POST SDP to a different URL.

title: Phase 1: Support Live YouTube Sources for Real-Time Transcription Pipeline
body:
# Phase 1: Support Live YouTube Sources for Real-Time Transcription Pipeline

## Overview

Currently `susi_translator` supports real-time audio transcription from live HLS streams. The next objective is to extend the pipeline to support **YouTube Live URLs as an input source**.

This issue represents **Phase 1** of a larger integration effort between `eventyay-interpretation` and `susi_translator`.

Initially:

- The media source will be a manually supplied **YouTube Live URL**
- Audio from the stream should be extracted and fed into the existing transcription pipeline
- Generated transcript chunks should be exposed for consumption by external systems

Future phases will replace the manual YouTube URL flow with direct Eventyay stream integration.

---

## Current Architecture

```text
HLS Stream
    ↓
Audio Chunking
    ↓
Transcription Engine
    ↓
Transcript Output
```

---

## Proposed Phase 1 Architecture

```text
YouTube Live URL
        ↓
Stream Extraction Layer
        ↓
Audio Processing
        ↓
Chunk Generation
        ↓
Existing SUSI Transcription Pipeline
        ↓
Live Transcript Chunks
        ↓
API / WebSocket Output
```

---

## Scope

### Phase 1A: Accept YouTube URL Input

Tasks:

- Add endpoint for receiving live YouTube URLs

Example:

```http
POST /stream/start

{
    "source_type": "youtube",
    "url": "https://youtube.com/live/example"
}
```

- Validate URL input
- Handle invalid URLs
- Handle unavailable streams
- Create stream session metadata

---

### Phase 1B: Stream Extraction Layer

Tasks:

- Extract audio from YouTube Live stream
- Convert extracted stream into compatible input for existing processing flow
- Handle reconnections and interruptions
- Maintain continuous streaming session

---

### Phase 1C: Integrate with Existing Transcription Pipeline

Tasks:

- Reuse current chunking logic
- Feed processed audio into current transcription system
- Ensure no regression in existing HLS functionality
- Generate live transcript chunks

---

### Phase 1D: Transcript Output Interface

Tasks:

Expose transcript chunks via:

- API endpoint
- WebSocket stream

Expected output:

```json
{
    "chunk_id": 1,
    "timestamp": "00:00:15",
    "text": "Welcome everyone to today's session"
}
```

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- Live YouTube URLs can be submitted
- Audio extraction functions correctly
- Existing HLS functionality remains unaffected
- Live transcript chunks are generated
- Transcript output is exposed via API/WebSocket
- Stream interruptions are handled gracefully

---

## Future Scope (Out of Current Phase)

### Phase 2

Replace manual URL input with Eventyay stream sources

```text
Eventyay Stream
        ↓
SUSI Processing Pipeline
        ↓
Transcription
```

---

### Phase 3

Enable real-time multilingual translation

```text
Transcript Chunks
        ↓
Translation Engine
        ↓
Language Specific Outputs
```

---

## Child Issues

- [ ] Add YouTube URL API endpoint
- [ ] Implement stream extraction layer
- [ ] Integrate extracted audio with existing chunking pipeline
- [ ] Add transcript output API/WebSocket
- [ ] Add test coverage

## Goal

### MediaMTX variables

title: [Phase 6][Step 3] Configure Nginx reverse proxy
body:
## Goal

Create the reverse proxy configuration that proxies all interpretation services, handles CORS, WebSocket upgrades, and WHIP/WHEP proxying.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 9.3. The reverse proxy terminates TLS and routes requests to portal (WebSocket), MediaMTX WHIP/WHEP signaling, and optionally HLS endpoints. CORS headers are needed for cross-origin WHEP playback from the Eventyay viewer.

## Scope

- Create reverse proxy config (Caddy preferred, Nginx alternative):
  - `/interpretation/ws/` → WebSocket proxy to portal:5000
  - `/interpretation/api/` → HTTP proxy to portal:5000
  - `/interpretation/whip/` → WHIP proxy to mediamtx:8889
  - `/interpretation/whep/` → WHEP proxy to mediamtx:8889 (primary listener path)
  - `/interpretation/hls/` → HLS proxy to mediamtx:8888 (fallback, until Phase 9 removal)
- CORS headers on WHEP and HLS responses (for cross-origin Eventyay viewer)
- WebSocket upgrade handling for portal connections
- TLS termination (Caddy auto-HTTPS or Nginx with Let's Encrypt)
- Rate limiting on WHIP publish endpoints

## Technical Notes

Infrastructure:
- `Caddyfile` or `nginx/interpretation.conf` — new config file
- `docker-compose.interpretation.yml` — proxy service definition

**Key:** WHEP is the primary listener path. HLS proxy is kept until Phase 9 (HLS removal).

## Tasks

title: Build viewer-side language selector
body:
## Goal

Add a language selector to the Eventyay talk/schedule viewer page so audience members can pick an interpretation language and hear live audio via WHEP (primary) or HLS (fallback).

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 8.4. A new template partial on the viewer page reads `config.interpretation_tracks` and renders a language selector + audio playback. Uses WHEP (WebRTC) for sub-second latency with HLS fallback via hls.js.

## Scope

- Django template partial for language selector:
  - Label: "🎧 Interpretation language:"
  - `<select>` with "— Original (floor) —" default + one option per language
  - Hidden `<audio>` element for HLS fallback playback
- JavaScript (plain ES module, no jQuery, no build step):
  - On language select: attempt WHEP playback first (WebRTC, sub-second latency)
  - If WHEP fails: fall back to HLS via hls.js (Chrome/Firefox) or native (Safari)
  - On "Original": stop interpretation audio
  - Auto-play on selection
- Load hls.js from CDN (or vendor locally) for HLS fallback only
- CORS must be configured on Nginx/Caddy for WHEP and HLS responses

## Technical Notes

Frontend (Eventyay main platform):
- `app/eventyay/schedule/templates/` or equivalent viewer template (add partial)
- `app/eventyay/static/eventyay/js/interpretation-player.js` — **new** ES module

**Playback priority:**
1. **WHEP** (WebRTC) — sub-second latency, works in Chrome, Firefox, Edge
2. **HLS** (hls.js) — ~3s latency fallback for Safari/iOS/older browsers
3. **Native HLS** — Safari/iOS native `<audio>` element

## Tasks

- [ ] Create Django template partial for language selector
- [ ] Create `interpretation-player.js` ES module
- [ ] Implement WHEP WebRTC playback (primary path)
- [ ] Implement HLS fallback via hls.js

title: Implement Portal to Eventyay API bridge
body:
## Goal

When a booth goes live, the interpretation portal calls the Eventyay REST API to register the WHEP + HLS URLs in the corresponding StreamSchedule entry.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 8.3. The portal calls `PATCH /api/v1/organizer/{organizer}/events/{event}/rooms/{room}/stream-schedules/{id}/` to register stream URLs. This closes the loop: booth goes live → stream URLs appear in Eventyay automatically.

## Scope

- Portal sends PATCH to Eventyay when a stream starts/stops publishing
- Payload updates `config.interpretation_tracks` with WHEP + HLS URLs per language
- **WHEP URL** is the primary playback URL (sub-second latency)
- **HLS URL** is the fallback for browsers without WebRTC
- URLs derived from MediaMTX path: `make_mediamtx_path(event_slug, language_code)`
- Requires `EVENTYAY_API_BASE` and `EVENTYAY_API_TOKEN` configuration
- Triggered by MediaMTX publish webhook or booth state change
- Graceful degradation: if Eventyay API is unreachable, portal continues to function
- **Simpler alternative for Phase 5:** organiser manually pastes URLs in Eventyay admin

## Technical Notes

Backend (Interpretation Portal):
- `portal/eventyay_bridge.py` — **new** file: API client using `httpx`
- `portal/config.py` — add `EVENTYAY_API_BASE`, `EVENTYAY_API_TOKEN` settings
- `fastapi_app.py` — trigger bridge on stream state change

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `portal/eventyay_bridge.py` with `httpx` API client

- [ ] Implement `unregister_stream_urls(event_slug, room_id, language)` for stream stop
- [ ] Call bridge when booth ingest state changes to live
- [ ] Call bridge when booth ingest stops
- [ ] Handle API errors gracefully (log warning, continue operation)
- [ ] Add timeout and retry logic for API calls
- [ ] Test with mock Eventyay API
- [ ] Document manual alternative (paste URL in admin)

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40

## Blockers

- Eventyay API must accept interpretation_tracks in config

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Portal registers WHEP + HLS URLs in Eventyay when booth goes live
- [ ] Portal unregisters URLs when booth stops

title: Extend StreamSchedule config for multi-language audio tracks
body:
## Goal

Use the existing `StreamSchedule.config` JSONField to store interpretation track WHEP + HLS URLs per language, enabling multi-language audio selection on the viewer page.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 8.2. The `config` JSONField on `StreamSchedule` is the designated extension point. No schema migration needed — store interpretation track URLs in a standardized JSON structure.

## Scope

- Define the `interpretation_tracks` JSON structure:
  ```json
  {
    "interpretation_tracks": {
      "en": {
        "whep": "https://media.domain/pycon-2026/en/whep",
        "hls": "https://media.domain/pycon-2026/en/index.m3u8"
      },
      "es": {
        "whep": "https://media.domain/pycon-2026/es/whep",
        "hls": "https://media.domain/pycon-2026/es/index.m3u8"
      }
    }
  }
  ```
- **WHEP is the primary playback URL** (sub-second latency via WebRTC)
- **HLS is the fallback** for browsers/devices without WebRTC support
- The main video stream (`url` field) remains the primary source
- Document the JSON schema for admin users
- Validate interpretation_tracks format when saving

## Technical Notes

Backend (Eventyay main platform):
- `app/eventyay/base/models/stream_schedule.py` (document config schema usage)
- `app/eventyay/api/views/stream_schedule.py` (validate interpretation_tracks on save)

**URL derivation:** Both WHEP and HLS URLs are derived from the MediaMTX path:
- WHEP: `{MEDIAMTX_WHEP_BASE}/{event_slug}/{language_code}/whep`
- HLS: `{MEDIAMTX_HLS_BASE}/{event_slug}/{language_code}/index.m3u8`

## Tasks

- [ ] Define and document `interpretation_tracks` JSON schema (WHEP + HLS per language)
- [ ] Add validation for interpretation_tracks format in API
- [ ] Ensure config field accepts and preserves interpretation_tracks
- [ ] Add example data for testing

- [ ] Document how to add interpretation tracks via admin/API

## Blockers

None — uses existing JSONField, no migration needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `interpretation_tracks` can be stored in StreamSchedule.config
- [ ] Each language entry has both `whep` and `hls` URLs
- [ ] API accepts PATCH with interpretation_tracks in config
- [ ] Existing config data is preserved (not overwritten)
- [ ] JSON format is validated
- [ ] No database migration required

title: [Phase 3][Step 6] Implement RBAC enforcement in portal routes
body:
## Goal

Guard every interpreter-facing and admin route with JWT-based role enforcement via FastAPI dependency injection.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 6.5. Every route is guarded via FastAPI dependency injection.

## Current State (Phase 2 baseline)

- `portal/auth.py` already has `verify_bearer()` and `verify_ws_token()` for basic token validation
- `fastapi_app.py` has `_require_access()` helper that calls `verify_bearer()`
- WebSocket auth via `verify_ws_token()` with 4001 close code on failure
- Phase 3 Step 1 (#63) adds role definitions, Step 3 (#65) adds role claims to JWT

## Scope

- Implement `get_current_participant(request)` — decode JWT from session cookie, return participant with role
- Implement `require_role(*roles)` — dependency factory that checks `participant.role in allowed_roles`
- Implement `require_admin()` — dependency for superadmin routes (checks `is_admin` JWT claim)
- Guard interpreter page with `require_role("interpreter", "coordinator", "listener")`
- Guard booth WebSocket with JWT validation from cookie or query param
- Enforce booth scoping: participant can only access their assigned booth
- Close WebSocket with code 4001 (auth) or 4003 (wrong booth) on failure
- Guard admin routes with `require_admin()`

## Technical Notes

**Modified files:**
- `portal/auth.py` — add `get_current_participant()`, `require_role()`, `require_admin()` (extends existing code)
- `fastapi_app.py` — apply dependencies to all routes

**Builds on existing code:**
- `_require_access()` in `fastapi_app.py` — evolves into proper RBAC
- `verify_ws_token()` in `portal/auth.py` — extended with role extraction
- `verify_bearer()` — extended with participant context

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement `get_current_participant()` with JWT decode from cookie
- [ ] Implement `require_role()` dependency factory
- [ ] Implement `require_admin()` dependency
- [ ] Apply role guard to interpreter page route
- [ ] Apply JWT validation to WebSocket endpoint (cookie or query param)
- [ ] Enforce booth_id scoping (participant.booth_id == requested booth)
- [ ] Apply admin guard to all `/admin/` routes
- [ ] Return proper error codes: 401 (invalid session), 403 (insufficient role)
- [ ] Close WebSocket with 4001/4003 codes on auth failure
- [ ] Add tests for all RBAC enforcement scenarios

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #65 (Invite-token auth — JWT issued with role claims)
- #63 (Role model — role definitions)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unauthenticated user cannot access interpreter page (redirected to error)
- [ ] Interpreter with Spanish booth token cannot access English booth (403)
- [ ] Listener cannot trigger "Go Live" — button absent from their UI
- [ ] Admin routes return 403 for non-admin users
- [ ] WebSocket rejects connections with invalid/missing JWT
- [ ] Tests cover all role-route combinations

## Out of Scope

- WHIP authentication tokens (deferred, Section 11.1 in RFC)
- Per-event admin scoping (event_admin sees only their event — future enhancement)

title: [Phase 3][Step 4] Build admin panel routes
body:
## Goal

Build the server-rendered Jinja2 admin panel for managing Events → Rooms → Booths hierarchy with live status display and WHEP listener URLs.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 6.4. The admin panel is plain Jinja2 templates with FastAPI backend routes and admin guard dependency injection. No separate admin framework.

## Scope

Admin routes:
- `GET /admin/` — Dashboard: event list + live booth status
- `GET /admin/events/` — Event list
- `POST /admin/events/` — Create event
- `GET /admin/events/{event_id}/` — Event detail: rooms, booths, live status
- `POST /admin/events/{event_id}/delete` — Delete event
- `GET /admin/events/{event_id}/rooms/` — Room list
- `POST /admin/events/{event_id}/rooms/` — Create room
- `GET /admin/events/{event_id}/rooms/{room_id}/` — Room detail: booth list
- `POST /admin/events/{event_id}/rooms/{room_id}/delete` — Delete room
- `GET /admin/events/{event_id}/rooms/{room_id}/booths/` — Booth list
- `POST /admin/events/{event_id}/rooms/{room_id}/booths/` — Create booth

title: [Phase 3][Step 3] Implement invite-token authentication flow
body:
## Goal

Implement the invite-token join flow: `GET /join/{token}` validates the token, issues a JWT cookie with role claims, and redirects to the correct booth page.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 6.3. Participants join via invite links — no passwords, no registration. The invite link IS the credential.

## Current State (Phase 2 baseline)

- `portal/auth.py` already has `create_token()`, `decode_token()`, `verify_bearer()`, `verify_ws_token()` using **PyJWT** (already installed)
- JWT secret configured via `portal/config.py` (`effective_jwt_secret`)
- WebSocket token validation exists in `verify_ws_token()` with 4001 close code
- Bearer token validation exists in `verify_bearer()`

## Scope

- `GET /join/{token}` route:
  1. Look up token in `invite_tokens` table
  2. Validate: not expired (`expires_at`), not used (`used_at`)
  3. Mark token as used (`used_at = now`)
  4. Issue signed JWT cookie: `{ participant_id, booth_id, role, event_slug, language_code }`
  5. Redirect to `/interpreter/{event_slug}/{language_code}` — role pre-set
- Add `create_participant_token()` to `portal/auth.py` for role-bearing JWTs
- Extend existing auth — do not replace

## Key Design Decisions

- **Redirect uses `event_slug/language_code`** (not `event_id/booth_id`) — consistent with Phase 2 URL patterns
- **PyJWT already installed** — no new dependency
- **Extend, do not replace** existing `portal/auth.py` functions
- **One-time tokens:** once used (`used_at` set), cannot be reused. JWT cookie is the ongoing credential.

## Technical Notes

**Modified files:**
- `portal/auth.py` — add `create_participant_token(participant_id, booth_id, role, event_slug, language_code)`
- `fastapi_app.py` — add `GET /join/{token}` route

**Uses:**
- `portal/database.py` — token lookup and mark-as-used
- `portal/models.py` — `InviteToken` model

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `create_participant_token()` to `portal/auth.py` with role claims
- [ ] Add `GET /join/{token}` route to `fastapi_app.py`
- [ ] Validate token: exists, not expired, not used
- [ ] Mark token as used on successful join
- [ ] Set JWT cookie on response
- [ ] Redirect to `/interpreter/{event_slug}/{language_code}`
- [ ] Handle errors: invalid token (404), expired (403), already used (403)
- [ ] Add tests for join flow (happy path + error cases)

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #64 (Database schema — for `InviteToken` model and CRUD)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Valid invite link redirects to correct booth page with JWT cookie
- [ ] JWT cookie contains `role`, `event_slug`, `language_code`, `booth_id` claims
- [ ] Expired tokens return 403
- [ ] Already-used tokens return 403
- [ ] Invalid tokens return 404
- [ ] Redirect URL uses `/interpreter/{event_slug}/{language_code}` pattern

## Out of Scope

- Admin panel (Step 4, #66)
- Token generation UI (Step 5, #67)
- RBAC enforcement on routes (Step 6, #68)
- Superadmin password auth (Step 7, #69)

title: [Phase 3][Step 2] Implement database schema (SQLAlchemy + Alembic)
body:
## Goal

Implement persistent database schema for events, rooms, booths, and invite tokens using SQLAlchemy ORM with Alembic migrations.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 6.2. The portal currently uses an in-memory booth registry (`portal/booth_state.py`). Phase 3 adds persistent storage for admin-managed entities while keeping the in-memory registry for runtime state.

## Current State (Phase 2 baseline)

- `portal/booth_state.py` has `Booth` and `Participant` dataclasses (in-memory, runtime state)
- `portal/booth_identity.py` provides `make_mediamtx_path()`, `make_booth_id()`, `parse_booth_id()` — these **derive** `mediamtx_path` from `event_slug + language_code`
- PyJWT already installed; Pydantic BaseSettings in `portal/config.py`
- Stack: FastAPI + Pydantic + uvicorn (Python 3.13)

## Scope

- Add SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async engine) and Alembic to dependencies
- Create `portal/models.py` with declarative models:
  - `Event` — slug (unique, indexed), display_name, created_at
  - `Room` — event FK, display_name, eventyay_room_id (nullable)
  - `DBBooth` — room FK, event FK, language_code, language_name (**NO** `mediamtx_path` column, **NO** `hls_url` column — both derived at runtime)
  - `InviteToken` — token (PK, 64-char hex), booth FK, role, label, expires_at, used_at, created_by
- Create `portal/database.py` with async session factory and CRUD helpers
- Initialize Alembic with initial migration
- SQLite for dev, PostgreSQL for prod (configurable via `portal/config.py`)

## Key Design Decisions

- **`mediamtx_path` is NOT stored.** Derived via `make_mediamtx_path(event.slug, language_code)` from `portal/booth_identity.py`. Single source of truth.
- **`hls_url` is NOT stored.** HLS is a fallback — URL derived from MediaMTX path. WHEP is primary playback.
- **Model name `DBBooth`** avoids collision with existing `Booth` dataclass in `booth_state.py`.
- **ORM over raw SQL:** SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic, not plain `sqlite3`.

## Technical Notes

**New files:**
- `portal/models.py` — SQLAlchemy declarative models
- `portal/database.py` — async session factory, CRUD helpers
- `alembic/` — migration directory
- `alembic.ini` — Alembic config

**Modified files:**
- `portal/config.py` — add `DATABASE_URL` setting
- `pyproject.toml` — add `sqlalchemy`, `alembic`, `aiosqlite` dependencies

## Tasks

- [ ] Add SQLAlchemy 2.0, Alembic, aiosqlite to `pyproject.toml`
- [ ] Create `portal/models.py` with Event, Room, DBBooth, InviteToken
- [ ] Create `portal/database.py` with async session factory
- [ ] Add `DATABASE_URL` to `portal/config.py`
- [ ] Initialize Alembic and create initial migration
- [ ] Add CRUD helpers for each model
- [ ] Add property on DBBooth to derive `mediamtx_path` via `make_mediamtx_path()`
- [ ] Add tests for model creation and CRUD
- [ ] Ensure all existing Phase 2 tests pass

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #63 (Role model — for `ParticipantRole` values in InviteToken.role)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All four tables created via Alembic migration
- [ ] `DBBooth` derives `mediamtx_path` at runtime (not stored)
- [ ] No `hls_url` column in any table
- [ ] CRUD operations work for all models
- [ ] Database URL configurable via environment variable
- [ ] All existing Phase 2 tests pass

## Out of Scope

- Admin panel routes (Step 4, #66)
- Token validation flow (Step 3, #65)
- Runtime booth registry changes (`booth_state.py` remains in-memory)

title: [Phase 3][Step 1] Define role model and permissions
body:
## Goal

Define the 5-role enum, permission helpers, and update the existing `Participant` dataclass to carry role metadata for RBAC enforcement.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 6.1. The portal already has a `ParticipantRole` type (`Literal["interpreter", "coordinator", "listener"]`) in `portal/booth_state.py` and JWT auth functions in `portal/auth.py`. Phase 3 extends these with two additional roles and permission helpers.

## Current State (Phase 2 baseline)

- `portal/booth_state.py` defines `ParticipantRole = Literal["interpreter", "coordinator", "listener"]`
- `Participant` dataclass has a `role: ParticipantRole` field
- `portal/auth.py` has `create_token()`, `decode_token()`, `verify_bearer()`, `verify_ws_token()` — PyJWT already installed
- Booth identity scheme in `portal/booth_identity.py` provides event-scoped naming
- 154+ tests passing across all modules

## Scope

- Extend `ParticipantRole` to include `event_admin` and `super_admin`
- Create `portal/roles.py` module with permission helpers:
  - `can_go_live(role)` → True for `interpreter` only
  - `can_set_active(role)` → True for `coordinator`, `event_admin`, `super_admin`
  - `can_manage_booths(role)` → True for `event_admin`, `super_admin`
  - `can_manage_events(role)` → True for `super_admin`
  - `is_admin_role(role)` → True for `event_admin`, `super_admin`
- Follow the Eventyay backend pattern from `core/permissions.py` for permission definitions
- Update `Participant` dataclass if needed for additional role metadata

## Technical Notes

**Extend** (do not replace):
- `portal/booth_state.py` — extend `ParticipantRole` type
- `portal/roles.py` — **new** module for permission helpers

**Pattern reference:**
- Eventyay backend uses `core/permissions.py` with enum-based permissions — follow similar pattern
- Keep permission checks as standalone functions, not class methods, for easy FastAPI dependency injection

## Tasks

- [ ] Extend `ParticipantRole` type to include `event_admin` and `super_admin`
- [ ] Create `portal/roles.py` with permission helper functions
- [ ] Add unit tests for all permission combinations
- [ ] Ensure existing Phase 2 tests still pass (154+ tests)

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #53 ✅ (Phase 2 booth state)
- #62 ✅ (Multi-event namespace isolation)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ParticipantRole` includes all 5 roles: `super_admin`, `event_admin`, `coordinator`, `interpreter`, `listener`
- [ ] Permission helpers return correct values for each role
- [ ] Existing `Participant` dataclass is backward-compatible
- [ ] All existing Phase 2 tests pass unchanged

## Out of Scope

- JWT payload changes (Step 3, #65)
- Database models (Step 2, #64)
- Route guards (Step 6, #68)

title: [Phase 2][Step 5] Add multi-event namespace isolation
body:
## Goal

Ensure each event gets its own namespace in MediaMTX paths with no cross-event interference. An organiser for one event cannot see or affect paths for another event.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 5.5. MediaMTX paths use `{event_slug}/{language_code}` structure. Each event is isolated at the path level. The portal must enforce this isolation in its API and state management.

## Scope

- Ensure MediaMTX paths are scoped by event_slug
- Portal API endpoints validate event context in all operations
- Booth state queries are scoped to the requesting event
- Prevent cross-event state leaks in BoothRegistry
- Add tests for namespace isolation

## Technical Notes

Backend:
- `portal/booth_state.py` (event-scoped queries)
- `fastapi_app.py` or `app.py` (event validation in routes)

## Tasks

- [ ] Scope BoothRegistry queries by event_slug
- [ ] Add event_slug validation to all booth API endpoints
- [ ] Prevent booth listing from leaking other events booths
- [ ] Verify MediaMTX path isolation (separate event prefixes)
- [ ] Add integration tests for cross-event isolation
- [ ] Test that event A participants cannot join event B booths

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #53 [Phase 2][Step 1] Booth identity schema
- #59 [Phase 2][Step 2] Updated booth state model

## Blockers

- Booth identity schema must include event_slug

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Event A booths are invisible to Event B API calls
- [ ] MediaMTX paths are prefixed by event_slug
- [ ] Booth state queries are event-scoped
- [ ] Cross-event join attempts are rejected with 403
- [ ] Integration tests verify isolation

## Out of Scope

- Per-event authentication (Phase 3)
- Admin multi-event management UI (Phase 3)

title: [Phase 2][Step 4] Implement booth bootstrap flow
body:
## Goal

Implement the end-to-end flow from booth creation via API to interpreter going live: organiser creates booth → interpreter joins via URL → coordinator assigns active → interpreter goes live via WHIP.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 5.4. Defines the complete lifecycle:
1. API call creates booth with event/language/room metadata
2. Interpreter navigates to booth URL
3. Coordinator assigns active interpreter
4. Active interpreter clicks "Go Live" and portal validates role before returning WHIP URL
5. HLS becomes available

## Scope

- Add `POST /api/events/{event_slug}/booths` endpoint to create booths
- Serve booth page at `/interpreter/{event_slug}/{language_code}`
- Portal validates active role before allowing "Go Live"
- Return WHIP URL: `{mediamtx_url}/whip/{event_slug}/{language_code}`
- Update booth page template to use event/language URL structure
- Add booth listing endpoint for admin/coordinator use

## Technical Notes

Backend:
- `fastapi_app.py` or `app.py` (booth creation endpoint, booth page route)
- `portal/booth_state.py` (booth creation with event context)

Frontend:
- `templates/interpreter_booth.html` (update URL structure)
- `static/js/interpreter-booth.js` (WHIP URL from booth context)

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `POST /api/events/{event_slug}/booths` endpoint
- [ ] Update booth page route to `/interpreter/{event_slug}/{language_code}`
- [ ] Validate active interpreter role before returning WHIP URL
- [ ] Pass WHIP URL as template variable derived from event/language
- [ ] Add booth listing endpoint `GET /api/events/{event_slug}/booths`
- [ ] Test full bootstrap flow end-to-end
- [ ] Update existing booth routes for backward compatibility

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #53 [Phase 2][Step 1] Booth identity schema
- #59 [Phase 2][Step 2] Updated booth state model

## Blockers

- Booth identity schema and state model must be in place

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Booth created via API with event_slug, language_code, room_id
- [ ] Interpreter accesses booth at `/interpreter/{event_slug}/{lang}`
- [ ] Only active interpreter can trigger "Go Live"
- [ ] WHIP URL matches `{mediamtx}/whip/{event_slug}/{language_code}`
- [ ] HLS output appears at correct path

## Out of Scope

title: [Phase 2][Step 3] Implement multi-layer active-interpreter enforcement
body:
## Goal

Implement three-layer enforcement ensuring only one interpreter can publish audio per language per event: portal booth state, portal API route, and MediaMTX single-publisher mode.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 5.3. Three independent layers prevent race conditions:
- Layer 1: `booth_state.py` — only active interpreter role can set `mic_active=True`
- Layer 2: Portal `/api/booth` route — returns WHIP URL only for active interpreter
- Layer 3: MediaMTX — rejects second WHIP publisher on same path

## Scope

- Layer 1: Verify/strengthen `update_participant_state()` enforcement in booth_state.py
- Layer 2: Add WHIP URL endpoint that checks active interpreter status before returning URL

Backend:

title: [Phase 2][Step 1] Define booth identity schema
body:
## Goal

Define the three-coordinate booth identity scheme: `{event_slug}/{language_code}/{booth_instance}`, mapping booth IDs to MediaMTX paths.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 5.1. A booth is identified by three coordinates. The MediaMTX path uses `{event_slug}/{language_code}` (one active stream per language per event). The portal booth ID is `{event_slug}-{language_code}`.

## Scope

- Define booth ID format: `{event_slug}-{language_code}` (e.g., `pycon2026-en`)
- Define MediaMTX path format: `{event_slug}/{language_code}`
- Support booth instances (Primary/Backup) — only one instance publishes at a time
- Define naming conventions and validation rules for event slugs and language codes (ISO 639-1)
- Update `BoothRegistry` to use the new identity scheme

## Technical Notes

Backend:
- `portal/booth_state.py` (update Booth dataclass, ID generation)
- `portal/config.py` (if new settings needed)

## Tasks

- [ ] Define booth ID format and MediaMTX path mapping
- [ ] Add validation for event_slug (alphanumeric + hyphens)
- [ ] Add validation for language_code (ISO 639-1)
- [ ] Update Booth dataclass with new identity fields
- [ ] Add helper function to convert booth_id ↔ MediaMTX path
- [ ] Update existing tests for new identity scheme
- [ ] Document naming conventions

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- Phase 1 complete (MediaMTX and WHIP working)

## Blockers

None — schema design can begin during Phase 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Booth IDs follow `{event_slug}-{language_code}` format
- [ ] MediaMTX paths follow `{event_slug}/{language_code}` format
- [ ] Invalid slugs/codes are rejected with clear error messages
- [ ] Booth ID ↔ MediaMTX path conversion works bidirectionally

## Out of Scope

- Database persistence (Phase 3)
- Admin UI for booth creation (Phase 3)

title: [Phase 1][Migration 1C] Migrate features from Flask/Socket.IO to FastAPI/WebSocket

labels.name: phase-1
labels.description: Phase 1: Local Media Pipeline + Interpreter Controls

body:
## Goal

Gradually move each coordination feature from Flask/Socket.IO to FastAPI/WebSocket. Update the frontend to use native WebSocket for each migrated feature.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Planned Migration section Phase 1C. Each feature is migrated individually, tested, and validated before moving to the next. Frontend switches from `socket.io-client` to native `WebSocket` per feature.

## Scope

Migrate the following features in order:

1. **Booth join/leave** — WebSocket `booth:join` / `booth:leave` messages in FastAPI
2. **Chat** — `booth:chat` via FastAPI WebSocket broadcast
3. **Participant state updates** — `booth:update-state` via FastAPI
4. **Relay handoff / active interpreter** — `booth:set-active` via FastAPI
5. **Auth** — Replace `BOOTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` with JWT-based auth middleware
6. **REST endpoints** — Port `/api/booth/`, `/api/interpreter/` routes from Flask to FastAPI

After each feature migration:
- Update frontend to use native `WebSocket` for that feature
- Run integration tests against FastAPI
- Remove the corresponding Flask handler only after tests pass

## Technical Notes

Backend:
- `fastapi_app.py` (add WebSocket handlers for each event type)
- `portal/auth.py` (new — JWT auth middleware)
- `app.py` (remove handlers after migration, per feature)

Frontend:
- `static/js/interpreter-booth.js` (replace socket.io calls with WebSocket)
- `templates/interpreter_booth.html` (remove socket.io-client script tag)

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement `booth:join` / `booth:leave` in FastAPI WebSocket handler
- [ ] Implement `booth:chat` broadcast in FastAPI
- [ ] Implement `booth:update-state` in FastAPI
- [ ] Implement `booth:set-active` in FastAPI
- [ ] Add JWT auth middleware for WebSocket connections
- [ ] Port REST `/api/booth/` endpoints to FastAPI
- [ ] Port REST `/api/interpreter/` endpoints to FastAPI
- [ ] Update frontend to use native WebSocket (per migrated feature)
- [ ] Add integration tests for each migrated endpoint
- [ ] Remove migrated Flask handlers after tests pass

## Dependencies

Depends on:
- Parent issue #40
- #50 [Phase 1][Migration 1B] FastAPI running alongside Flask

## Blockers

- FastAPI must be running and have WebSocket endpoint scaffolding (#50)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All Socket.IO events are handled by FastAPI WebSocket
- [ ] Frontend uses native WebSocket for all coordination
- [ ] JWT auth validates WebSocket connections
- [ ] All REST endpoints work on FastAPI
- [ ] Integration tests pass for all migrated features
- [ ] Flask handlers removed for migrated features

## Out of Scope

- Removing Flask entirely (Phase 1D)
- Removing socket.io-client from package.json (Phase 1D)
- Admin panel (Phase 3)

## Goal

Implement automated preflight checks that validate mic permission, audio device availability, and media server reachability before allowing the interpreter to go live.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 4.1 Step 6. Before showing "Go Live", the portal runs automated checks and displays pass/fail status. The "Continue to Booth" (or "Go Live") button is disabled until critical checks pass.

## Scope

  1. Microphone permission (attempt `getUserMedia`, catch denial)
  2. Audio device detected (at least one `audioinput` in `enumerateDevices()`)
  3. MediaMTX reachable (fetch HLS base URL)
- Display each check with ✅/❌/⚠️ status
- Disable "Go Live" button until mic permission and server reachability pass
- Show inline error messages for failures with troubleshooting hints

## Goal

Allow interpreters to select which audio input device to use (headset mic, USB interface, etc.) via a dropdown, and display a real-time mic level meter to confirm the device is working.

## Background

From parent RFC issue #40, Section 4.1 Step 4. Currently `getUserMedia` uses the browser default device with no UI to change it. Interpreters need explicit device selection and visual confirmation before going live.

## Scope
